title: Name who approves the go and who can start a rollback
summary: At 02:00, a rollback decision must be fast. The plan recommends that you approve the go against a written checklist, and that the on-call database lead can start a rollback alone.

badges.tip: Only you can give this authority.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: The cutover has two decision points. At 01:30, someone says go or no-go. After 02:00, someone must start a rollback if a check fails. Each minute of delay keeps the shop closed.

blocks.title: The go/no-go checklist
blocks.html:
• Two full rollback rehearsals passed in staging (F6).
  • The point-in-time recovery test passed (F6).
  • A load test at 1,450 writes/s for 2 hours passed, with a p95 write latency below 25 ms.
  • The CDC lag stayed below 5 s for the last 24 hours.
  • Row counts and checksums match on all 46 tables.
  • The support team and the on-call database lead are on call.

[src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: [UNVERIFIED] Nobody has tested the peak rate of 1,450 writes/s. If the load test fails, the go must be a no-go. The person who approves must accept this rule in advance.

options.label: You approve the go and each rollback
options.detail_html: Effect: one person holds all authority. Risk: medium. At 02:00, a rollback waits until you answer the phone.

options.label: You approve the go. The on-call database lead can start a rollback alone
options.detail_html: Effect: you approve the go at 01:30 against the checklist. After 02:00, the database lead starts a rollback without a call. Risk: low.

options.label: A change board approves on the Thursday before the cutover
options.detail_html: Effect: four people approve 3 days in advance. The on-call lead runs the night alone. Risk: medium. The approval is 3 days old, and the CDC lag and the checksums can change in that time.

recommendation_html: Option b. You keep the decision that needs judgement: the go. The person at the console gets the decision that needs speed: the rollback.
